title: Tableau AI: What It Is & How To Use It In 2026
summary: Tableau AI as of October 2026: what Pulse, Tableau Agent, Tableau Next and the Tableau MCP server do, which edition includes each, and their limits.
body_markdown:
## Tableau Pulse: metrics that come to you


Pulse is for people who don't open dashboards: a metric is defined once on a data source, people follow it, and Pulse sends each person a digest of insights by email and Slack ([Tableau help: About Tableau Pulse](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-gb/pulse_intro.htm) ). A definition is narrow by design: one measure with an aggregation, one time dimension and optional filters, such as the` SUM` of` Profit` over` Order Date` in the official MCP server's documentation ([tableau-mcp docs](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/tools/pulse/list-all-pulse-metric-definitions.md) ).


**Edition and price.** Tableau says Pulse is "included out-of-the-box with all Tableau Cloud and Embedded Analytics editions" ([Tableau Pulse](https://www.tableau.com/products/tableau-pulse) ), so the cost is the seat. The conversational part is extra: Tableau Agent in Pulse, renamed from Enhanced Q&A (also called Discover), needs Tableau+ outside a 60-day trial according to Tableau's help pages ([Try Tableau Pulse Enhanced Q&A](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/tableau_gai_trial.htm) ), and the current Cloud pricing page lists it under Cloud+ ([Tableau Cloud pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) ).


**Limits.** Pulse is Tableau Cloud only: "Tableau Server is unable to use Tableau Pulse at this time" ([tableau-config](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/configuration/tableau-config.md) ). It answers about metrics someone has already defined, and one measure over time suits KPIs such as revenue or tickets better than open-ended questions; a new breakdown or another data source goes back to a dashboard or an analyst.


## Tableau Agent: an assistant for authors


Tableau Agent, renamed from Einstein Copilot, helps you explore data, create visualizations, and create and explain calculations. It runs in Tableau Cloud web authoring, Tableau Desktop (2025.1 and later), Tableau Prep Builder (2025.2 and later) and Tableau Server (2025.3 and later) ([Tableau Agent FAQ](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein_faq.htm) ).


**Edition and price.** On Tableau Cloud, Tableau Agent comes with Cloud+ (or the Tableau+ Bundle), quoted by sales, for the Creator and Explorer roles, not Viewers, and Tableau picks the model. On Tableau Server, an administrator connects each site to your own OpenAI or Azure OpenAI account (localized help pages date Azure OpenAI support to Server 2026.2); those requests bypass Salesforce's Einstein Trust Layer and are billed by your provider ([Turn On AI in Your Tableau Server Site](https://help.tableau.com/current/server/en-us/sites_gai_server.htm) ,[AI in Tableau and Trust](https://help.tableau.com/current/tableau/en-gb/tableau_gai_einstein_trust.htm) ).


**Limits.** The FAQ aims it mainly at novice users and ad-hoc exploration inside a workbook. Dashboard Narratives work with published data sources only; cubes aren't supported; with data blending the agent uses only the primary data source; and live connections make it slower, so Tableau recommends extracts or file-based data.


## Tableau Next: Salesforce's agentic analytics app


Tableau Next is a separate product line from Tableau Cloud and Server, so your existing workbooks stay where they are. It reads data from Salesforce Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud), which can hold the data or reference external sources, and puts Tableau Semantics, its semantic layer, between that data and its agents ([Tableau Next Overview](https://help.tableau.com/current/tableau-next/en-us/tableau_next_overview.htm) ). The first agents, announced at TC25 in May 2025: Data Pro helps analysts build semantic models, Concierge creates visualizations from natural-language requests, and Inspector monitors metrics and alerts people to what drives a trend ([Tableau TC25 announcements](https://www.tableau.com/blog/top-10-announcements-keynote-tc25) ).


**Edition and price.** Tableau Next starts at $40 per user per month, billed annually, including Tableau Agent, Tableau Semantics and the native Slack integration ([Tableau Next pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/next) ); I couldn't find a published price for added Consumer licenses. It's sold standalone or in the Tableau+ Bundle, which adds Tableau Next and Data 360 to Cloud+ and is quoted by sales. Salesforce's pricing page says Tableau Next is now role-based, "eliminating consumption-based pricing (like Flex credits) for data queries, data transforms, and agentic analytics", while Data Services credits or Flex credits may still apply ([Salesforce: Tableau Next pricing](https://www.salesforce.com/analytics/pricing/tableau-next/) ).


**Limits.** It lives on the Salesforce platform. If your metric definitions already sit in dbt, LookML or a Power BI semantic model, check how they get into Tableau Semantics before you commit, or plan to maintain them in two places. Our[Tableau Next vs Dot comparison](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/tableau-vs-dot) collects early user reports.


## The Tableau MCP server


Tableau's official Model Context Protocol server, open source under Apache-2.0 at[github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp) , lets an MCP client such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Slack list and query your Tableau content, in two forms:


- **Hosted** at` https://mcp.tableau.com` , for Tableau Cloud. Users sign in with OAuth 2.1 under their own Tableau identity, so existing permissions apply. Tableau says it's "Available to Tableau Cloud customers on any SKU" and "Not available for Tableau Server" ([Hosted Tableau MCP](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/hosted-tableau-mcp/README.md) ).
- **Self-hosted** , from the` @tableau/mcp-server` npm package (Node.js 22.7.5 or later), Docker, or a standalone binary, for Tableau Cloud or Tableau Server.


### What it exposes


On October 29, 2026, the main branch on GitHub defines 55 tools for Tableau Cloud and Server, in 18 groups ([toolName.ts](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/src/tools/web/toolName.ts) ; the latest npm release may lag the main branch). The ones most people want:


- **datasource** :` list-datasources` ,` get-datasource-metadata` and` query-datasource` , which runs VizQL queries against published data sources: you pass fields, aggregations and filters as JSON, not SQL. Embedded (workbook) data sources need a site opt-in and Tableau 2026.3 or later ([query-datasource docs](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/tools/data-qna/query-datasource.md) ).
- **view** and **workbook** : list them, read a view's data or an image of it.
- **pulse** : seven tools for metrics, subscriptions and Pulse insights.
- **content-exploration** :` search-content` across the site.


The rest goes further than most people expect: publishing content, running Prep flows, managing users, deleting content and admin insights. A separate Desktop build drives a running copy of Tableau Desktop ([Desktop quickstart](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/README.desktop.md) ).


### How to set it up


On Tableau Cloud, add` https://mcp.tableau.com` as a remote MCP server in your client and sign in when prompted. For Tableau Server, or to control the configuration yourself, run it locally with a personal access token. A read-only setup with a row cap:


```text
{
"mcpServers": {
"tableau": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@tableau/mcp-server@latest"],
"env": {
"SERVER": "https://your-tableau-server.example.com",
"SITE_NAME": "your-site",
"PAT_NAME": "mcp-readonly",
"PAT_VALUE": "...",
"INCLUDE_TOOLS": "datasource,view,pulse,content-exploration,list-workbooks,get-workbook",
"MAX_RESULT_LIMIT": "1000"
}
}
}
}
```


The site needs the VizQL Data Service enabled, and users need the API Access permission on the data sources they query. The Metadata API should be on for metadata and lineage, and Pulse needs its AI features turned on ([Tableau configuration](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/configuration/tableau-config.md) ). Our Tableau MCP server guide has every client config and a shared-server setup.


### Limits and security considerations


- **Identity.** The hosted server acts as each signed-in user. A self-hosted server on a personal access token acts as that token's owner for everyone who uses it, so a shared deployment should use` oauth` or` direct-trust` auth ([environment variables](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/configuration/mcp-config/env-vars.md) ).
- **Where results go.** Tableau says "The hosted service does not store your Tableau data", but the rows a tool returns land in the context of whichever model your MCP client runs, so that provider's retention terms apply.
- **No row cap by default.**` MAX_RESULT_LIMIT` is empty (no limit) unless you set it;` MAX_RESULT_LIMITS` sets caps per tool.
- **Write tools exist.** Admin tools are off by default, but for a read-only assistant set` INCLUDE_TOOLS` . Site admins can't disable hosted MCP, only exclude tools for their site through the REST API.
- **Scope.**` INCLUDE_PROJECT_IDS` ,` INCLUDE_TAGS` and similar variables fence a server to certain content, though not the Pulse tools ([tool scoping](https://github.com/tableau/tableau-mcp/blob/main/docs/docs/configuration/mcp-config/tool-scoping.md) ).
- **Entitlements.** Pulse insight briefs and Tableau Knowledge need Tableau+, and the full Metadata API surface needs Data Management.
- **Telemetry** is on by default; set` PRODUCT_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` to turn it off.
- **The reasoning happens in the client.** Your client's model decides which fields to pull and how to read them, so answer quality depends on that model and on how well your published data sources are named and described.


### Tableau Next has its own MCP server


Salesforce documents a separate hosted MCP server for Tableau Next, at` https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/analytics/tableau-next` . Its tools read Tableau Semantics models and send a natural-language question to the Tableau Analytics Agent against a chosen model ([Salesforce: Tableau Next MCP](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/tableau-next.html) ). Tableau MCP connects to Tableau Cloud and Server; Tableau Next MCP connects to Tableau Next ([Trailhead](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/data-analytics-insights-powered-by-headless-360/deliver-data-analytics-anywhere-with-tableau-next-mcp) ).


## What happened to Ask Data, Explain Data and Tableau GPT


- **Ask Data** , Tableau's natural-language query feature, was retired in Tableau Cloud in February 2024 and in Tableau Server 2024.2, together with the legacy Metrics feature, which Pulse replaced ([Tableau help](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/ask_data_enable.htm) ).
- **Explain Data** is still available. It gives "AI-powered explanations to what might be driving unexpected mark values", has been open to all licensed users since 2021.2 ([Tableau blog](https://www.tableau.com/blog/bringing-power-explain-data-all-tableau-users) ), and is on by default, though admins can turn it off ([Tableau help](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/explain_data_enable.htm) ).
- **Data Stories** was retired in January 2025, with 2025.1 ([Tableau help](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/data_stories_configure_edit.htm) ).
- **Tableau GPT** was announced at TC 2023, built on Salesforce's Einstein GPT (developed with OpenAI), and Pulse was announced as built on it ([InterWorks](https://interworks.com/blog/2023/06/07/what-are-tableau-gpt-and-tableau-pulse/) ). Its shipping equivalents are Tableau Agent and Tableau Agent in Pulse.


For a Viewer, the closest thing to Ask Data today is Tableau Agent in Pulse (on Cloud+) or an AI client on the MCP server, given the API Access permission on the data source.
